item.title: Joe Scarborough goes after ESPN’s Pat McAfee: ‘It is a shame for the viewer’
item.description: Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” Joe Scarborough of “Morning Joe” hammered away at Tuesday during election day. McAfee’s recent headline-grabbing issues with the University of Utah was the tipping point. “I’ve just had enough of this Pat McAfee ruining ‘College GameDay,’” Scarborough said Tuesday. “I look forward to waking up on Saturday mornings and watching that. ... It’s like he’s melting down. ... “It’s really ESPN. I mean, they run their company the way they want to run their company, but man, it is a shame for the viewer.” It's election day in America, and Morning Joe spent over two minutes discussing the country's most pressing issue: Pat McAfee ruining College GameDay "I don't know if they haven't gotten the message yet, but the manosphere that we all thought was brought in in '24, it may get… pic.twitter.com/a16be985Zt — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 3, 2026 McAfee revealed there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversy surrounding ESPN’s “College GameDay” visit to Utah. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but ... I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee posted on X. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.” The post includes screenshots from direct messages threatening violence against him and tweets expressing a desire to see him dead. The issue, according to Scarborough, is the show has gotten away from college football being played on Saturday and it’s more about itself. “I love watching Rece (Davis),” he said. “I love watching those guys and watching Nick (Saban) on there talking. ... Meanwhile, McAfee said he felt “uncomfortable” after the University of Utah posted a since-deleted video of students “dogging” him. He also said the video shared by the university account was inciteful against him. McAfee cited the visit to the University of Utah reminded him of assassination of Charlie Kirk . Utah, for its part, apologized Monday. item.title: Report: Russell Wilson interviewing for NC State head coach position
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 07: Quarterback Russell Wilson #3 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up against the Los Angeles Rams at Lumen Field on October 07, 2021 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Steph Chambers Longtime Seahawks quarterback and current CBS Sports analyst Russell Wilson may have a new position -- at the collegiate level. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Super Bowl XLVIII champion interviewed for NC State football’s head coaching position Tuesday, Nov. 3. Wilson served as NC State’s starting quarterback for two years, before heading off to play at Wisconsin. Following his time in Wisconsin, Wilson played fourteen years in the NFL, with 10 of those years spent in Seattle. That being said, Wilson isn’t the only former NFL quarterback fighting for the position. Longtime Chargers quarterback Philip Rivers also interviewed for the head coaching job, according to ESPN. Like Wilson, Rivers also played for NC State, playing for the Wolfpack from 2000 to 2003.

item.title: KENS 5 sports anchor Nate Ryan announces surprise departure in San Antonio
item.description: KENS 5 sports anchor Nate Ryan has announced his sudden departure from the station. (Courtesy, KENS 5) A big shakeup is coming to San Antonio TV screens, particularly for local sports fans. KENS 5 evening sports anchor Nate Ryan, who many will recognize by his Spurs courtside coverage, announced he'll be leaving the station at the end of the week. In a Wednesday, November 4, Instagram post, the Chicago native gave a bit of "personal news." "It's been the ultimate privilege to represent this station, continuing a legacy that's spanned over 75 years," he said. "To have led the Sports Department for the last 4+ years is one of the honors of my life. Hopefully they were as much fun for you, as they were for me…..Every. Single. Night." He joined the local CBS affiliate in 2022 . Continuing, he said, "I got lucky when I came to KENS. They sat the kid next to Isis, Henry, and my man Billy T on the prime-time desk. The chemistry came quick. We've learned, we've listened, and we've definitely laughed. The memories we made on set I'll have forever." He also thanked the San Antonio community in his farewell post. "For as much as I've worked for the station, I work for the people of San Antonio," Ryan said. "The competitive spirit of our city sets it apart: From the Spurs, to our youth sports. San Antonio deserves an energy to match! Thank you for welcoming me into your city, and into your homes. Hopefully you still do in the future ;) My last newscast is this Thursday. Much more then." Ryan was tight-lipped about his next move in the post, though some commenters speculated about what's coming next or just wished him well. MySA reached out for additional info, but didn't immediately receive a response. Sign up for Afternoon Headlines, MySA's free newsletter bringing you San Antonio's top stories of the day. Green Bay Packers star linebacker Micah Parsons acknowledged Wednesday that he does not expect to immediately return to his All-Pro form following last year’s ACL injury , admitting that his conditioning and physical limitations remain significant obstacles. As the Packers (5-3) prepare for Sunday’s Week 9 road matchup against the New England Patriots (5-3) , Parsons offered a candid assessment of his recovery and expectations for the remainder of the season. The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman shared Parsons’ comments Wednesday on X, formerly known as Twitter. Parsons emphasized that while his performance might fluctuate, his effort and intensity will remain consistent as he works toward regaining his previous form. “My conditioning right now is probably the worst it’s been in my career, you know what I mean? And that’s just the reality of it. Am I gonna go out there and play 50, 60 snaps how I was doing before? Absolutely not. It’s just not realistic. My body’s not there yet. I don’t even think my knee’s built for that yet. I didn’t go through training camp.” The former All-Pro also acknowledged that returning to his previous level of production will require patience as he continues rebuilding his conditioning. “So am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person that I once was, this year? Probably not until later, after I go through all my phases and things like that,” Parsons said. I’m not scared of seeing the failure of this thing because you gotta (understand) I just came back from an 11-month injury,” Parsons said. His comments come as Green Bay looks to build momentum following its 27-19 Week 8 victory over the Carolina Panthers last Thursday. Prior to the start of the 2026 WNBA season, there were few pundits who picked the Golden State Valkyries to win the championship. During the Valkyries’ championship parade on Wednesday, Kiah Stokes showed up wearing a shirt that had a printout of ESPN’s analytics. ESPN ultimately responded to Kiah Stokes’ shirt by jokingly creating a new analytics chart showing the Valkyries as having 100 percent odds at winning the WNBA championship. They also clarified that they had given the Valkyries the top odds at winning it all as of Aug. 10. Jokes aside, Stokes was a huge factor in the Valkyries’ title run . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) During the regular season Stokes appeared in 43 of 44 games at a little over 22 minutes per game. She averaged 3.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.7 blocked shots with splits of 43.4 percent shooting from the field and 29 percent shooting from the 3-point line. In the playoffs, she averaged 4.2 points, 10.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 2.4 blocked shots while shooting 51.1 percent from the field, 23.5 percent from the 3-point line and 75 percent from the free-throw line. item.title: Giants should price a Dalvin Tomlinson reunion before deadline
item.description: Dec 28, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Arizona Cardinals defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (94) reacts after a play during the first half against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants have another week before the November 10 trade deadline. If they still want interior defensive help, a familiar name is worth a phone call: Dalvin Tomlinson. This recommendation is not a report that New York and the Chargers are negotiating. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell previously suggested Tomlinson as an option, as summarized here . Los Angeles controls whether the veteran is available and what it would accept. Sep 13, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (94) hugs Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) after the game at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Why Tomlinson could help the Giants Tomlinson played for the Giants from 2017 through 2020. The Chargers announced his agreement on a one-year deal this offseason after he started all 17 games for Arizona in 2025. His experience gives New York a possible rotational run defender without requiring it to chase a long-term commitment in a trade. The second part of the calculation is price. A rental on an expiring agreement should not cost a premium pick, particularly when New York could instead stay with its current group. The Giants should ask about a late-round price and the remaining salary before treating the idea as a real upgrade. The Associated Press reported Tuesday that Greg Newsome’s extension gives New York some cap flexibility ahead of the deadline. The report did not establish a Tomlinson pursuit or a specific amount available for a trade. Tomlinson dealt with a hamstring issue earlier this season; the Chargers later removed him from their injury report . New York would still need current medical information before agreeing to anything. An old injury update is not a current clearance. The sensible limit The alternative is to keep the rotation intact and retain the draft capital. That may be preferable if the Chargers value Tomlinson more highly than a short-term role justifies. The Giants should make the inquiry, not force a reunion. Availability, compensation and the player’s current health are all unknown, and those details determine whether the idea improves the roster. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. Instead, he’s leaving the Guardians’ organization entirely, one of 10 players to elect free agency from the Guards on Wednesday. Valera is the most eye-catching name of the group, a former high-ranking prospect who even had a clutch playoff home run on his MLB ledger in Cleveland before falling off and not making it back. The Guardians clearly have moved on, as it doesn’t seem like they did anything to keep Valera around. If Valera is going to make it back to MLB, it won’t be with Cleveland — at least it doesn’t seem that way right now. George Valera Decision Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO – OCTOBER 01: George Valera #35 of the Cleveland Guardians hits a home run during the first inning against the Detroit Tigers in game two of the American League Wild Card Series at Progressive Field on October 01, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) Valera was at the point of his contract where he could choose to “elect free agency,” and that’s what he did. Minor league ballplayers will rarely turn that choice down. After being under one organization’s control for half a decade or more, they want the chance to pursue new opportunities. It doesn’t preclude Valera from re-signing with the Guardians, but it does allow every other team who hasn’t had a crack to have Valera before to go after him if they’d like. Given Valera’s prospect pedigree and raw power, it seems possible he’ll get a look from another ballclub. They aren’t going to be making blockbuster signings, but they can still add players to improve their roster for 2027. Year one of their rebuild was largely a success from an organizational standpoint. They are still rebuilding, which is why they won’t make splashy moves, but they do have a foundation in place that they can soon start to supplement with some additional players. One thing they might want to look into is adding a short-term solution at third base while they wait for some of their prospects to develop. item.title: Travis Kelce Reveals True Feelings on Jonathan Taylor Amid Trade Rumors
item.description: Travis Kelce on Jonathan Taylor trade rumors Getty The Indianapolis Colts are approaching the NFL trade deadline amid a major roster shake-up. The team has already traded away veteran standouts Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, leaving running back Jonathan Taylor’s future increasingly uncertain as Indianapolis considers its next steps. Taylor remains one of the Colts’ most productive players, but the team’s 2-6 record has intensified questions about whether it should keep building around him or seek valuable draft capital. With the Nov. 10 deadline approaching, the three-time Pro Bowl running back has become a central name in trade discussions. Travis Kelce Urges Jonathan Taylor to Stay With the Indianapolis Colts During the New Heights podcast , Travis Kelce encouraged Taylor to remain with the Colts rather than pursue a move to a contender. “Indianapolis. Stay there, Jonathan. Go ahead. I mean, stay there. You only be in that one organization your whole life. Trust me, take it from two guys that have been there. It’s the best,” Kelce said. The brothers also considered potential destinations if Taylor were traded. Travis mentioned the Minnesota Vikings , while questioning whether their offense would make the move worthwhile for the running back. He also brought up the Seattle Seahawks , wondering whether they might pursue Taylor after moving on from Kenneth Walker III. Jason, however, returned to the idea that Taylor should stay in Indianapolis. Travis acknowledged his brother’s position, replying, “Stay there. Perfect. All right, I get it.” Taylor’s on-field production gives him significant value as the deadline nears. Through eight games, he has recorded 610 rushing yards, averaged 4.1 yards per carry, and scored eight rushing touchdowns. His eight-carry, 23-yard performance against Jacksonville was a difficult outing, but it does not erase his importance to the Colts’ offense. Indianapolis selected Taylor with the 41st overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August, keeping him under contract through 2028. That commitment makes him more than a short-term rental for a potential contender and adds another consideration to any trade. The Colts have already moved Nelson to Seattle and Buckner to San Francisco as they look to reshape the roster and collect draft capital. Taylor’s contract and production make his situation different, leaving Indianapolis to weigh his on-field value against what another team might offer. The Kelce brothers offered their perspective on Taylor’s future, but the Colts’ decision ultimately depends on the offers arriving before the deadline. item.description: Arteta says Gyokeres ‘needed’ his performance against Slavia Prague Mikel Arteta says Viktor Gyokeres “needed” a performance like he produced in the 2-1 Champions League win over Slavia Prague. item.title: Craig Luschenat on what player enhancement means to Boston Celtics
item.description: Craig Luschenat has made a name for himself with the Boston Celtics as one of the NBA's best player development coaches (or as they call such a position in the Celtics organization, a player enhancement coach). But much as Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla tends to do, Luschenat refuses to take sole credit for the successes we have seen with Boston in such an ambit, instead crediting the full bench of Boston assistants for any evident enhancements. As to the meaning behind using "player enhancement" instead of "player development," the Celtics assistant related that he does not "have a definition, that's for sure" in a recent interview with the team-produced "View From the Rafters" podcast. "I would just say it's our job to basically put a plan in place for each guy and then just try and execute that plan," added Luschenat. "I think we put big emphasis on how we can develop our guys," said the Celtics assistant. "We look at our guys from every different lens, from mental performance, strength, and conditioning (to) what the analytics say, what the film says, what the nutrition says." "And then we essentially try to put a plan in place and try and execute it. So … it's been a good few years here, but we don't have all the answers, and we're still trying to get better." item.title: Former Spurs forward Jeremy Sochan breaks silence after being cut by Trail Blazers
item.description: Former San Antonio Spurs forward Jeremy Sochan reflects on being cut by the Portland Trail Blazers and his next chapter with the Texas Legends. (Marvin Pfeiffer/San Antonio Express-News) Former San Antonio Spurs forward and NBA champion Jeremy Sochan isn't dwelling on his latest NBA setback. After being waived by the Portland Trail Blazers ahead of the 2026-27 season, the former Spurs first-round pick is looking to build on his experience rather than focus on another unexpected departure. Speaking during Texas Legends media day, Sochan reflected on his brief stint in Portland and explained why he remains optimistic about his basketball future. "I could look at it negatively, the Portland situation. But when I look back at that situation, I think the two months I was there, I grew a lot," Sochan said. The 23-year-old forward signed a one-year deal with Portland during the offseason but was released despite what he described as a productive preseason. Sochan said he remained healthy throughout training camp and made the most of his opportunities on the court. ALSO READ: Streaking Spurs brace for Mavericks' Irving-Flagg one-two punch "I was healthy throughout the whole training camp, preseason and open gym. So I think that was a blessing," Sochan said. "When we got into preseason games, the minutes I got I think I used them to the best of my ability. I had good games." Rather than allowing the setback to derail his progress, Sochan said he is focused on maintaining his momentum. "So, why would I hold weight on something that I can't control?" Sochan said. "And instead, be in this moment and do what I can do and keep that momentum going." Sochan's next opportunity will come with the Texas Legends, the Dallas Mavericks' NBA G League affiliate, which selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 G League Draft. The Legends are preparing for the G League season, which begins Friday, Nov. 6. Selected ninth overall by San Antonio in the 2022 NBA Draft, Sochan spent most of his NBA career with the Spurs before splitting the 2025-26 season between San Antonio and the New York Knicks. With the Knicks, he won a championship as they defeated the Spurs in last season's NBA Finals. He has averaged 9.9 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.5 assists during his NBA career. item.title: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Is On Track To Make NFL History
item.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is putting together a season that could place him among the most productive pass catchers in NFL history. The third-year standout is on pace to challenge Calvin Johnson’s single-season receiving record while pursuing the league’s first 2,000-yard receiving season. The wideout continued his historic campaign Monday night, recording six receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. The performance marked his seventh game with at least 100 receiving yards through the first eight contests, placing him in rare company during the Super Bowl era. Dec 18, 2025; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet (26) celebrates with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (11) after scoring a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams in the first half at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images The 24-year-old now has 985 receiving yards and nine touchdowns through eight games, putting him ahead of the rest of the NFL in receiving yardage. Smith-Njigba’s current average of 123.1 yards per game projects to approximately 2,093 yards over a 17-game schedule, a total that would surpass Johnson’s benchmark of 1,964 yards set with the Detroit Lions in 2012. Johnson averaged 122.8 receiving yards per game during his record-setting season, which took place when the NFL played 16 regular-season games. At his current pace, Smith-Njigba could break that mark before the end of the 16th game, potentially making the extra game unnecessary to reach the record. Only one player has reached 2,000 receiving yards in a season, and the Seahawks’ leading pass catcher would become the first to accomplish the feat if he maintains his production. Cooper Kupp came close in 2021, finishing with 1,947 yards for the Los Angeles Rams, just 17 short of Johnson’s record. Seattle’s offense has relied heavily on Smith-Njigba , whose production has continued despite opposing defenses focusing on limiting his impact. The Seahawks will need to sustain their passing-game efficiency and keep their star healthy as the schedule advances. With nine games remaining, the opportunity to rewrite the NFL record book remains within reach, although maintaining the current pace will be a significant challenge. item.title: Court opens possibility that NFL Sunday Ticket case could expand to YouTube TV
item.description: NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube. On Friday, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals issued a ruling overturning a judge’s decision to toss a jury verdict levied against the NFL over antitrust violations associated with its packaging of NFL Sunday Ticket to DirecTV. The case, which has been in the courts for about a decade, addressed whether the league violated antitrust law by compelling its Sunday Ticket provider, in this case DirecTV, to price the product artificially high so to protect the Sunday afternoon packages it sells to Fox and CBS. A jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs and the NFL was on the hook for $4.7 billion in damages, an amount that would be trebled to over $14 billion under federal antitrust statutes. But shortly after the jury reached its verdict, the judge overseeing the case tossed the ruling citing issues with how the plaintiffs’ expert witnesses calculated the damages. On Friday, a three-judge panel ruled on the plaintiffs’ subsequent appeal , deciding that the jury’s assessment that the NFL was liable for the antitrust violations would stand, but the amount the league owes in damages would be retried. But, according to a recent report by Puck’s legal expert Eriq Gardner , there’s another key ruling the panel of judges made that has been largely overlooked. Per Gardner, the judges filed a memorandum disposition that sent “injunction claims back to the district court to consider whether they remain viable now that the NFL’s deal with DirecTV has expired.” The ongoing case deals only with a period in which the NFL licensed Sunday Ticket to DirecTV. The league’s out-of-market package now, of course, is held by YouTube TV. And for all intents and purposes, NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV is following the exact same model that currently has the league in hot water. Sunday Ticket remains priced at a premium rate to protect the value of CBS’ and Fox’s Sunday afternoon packages. Gardner suggests that sending the injunction claims back to he district court opens the possibility for those claims to be extended to YouTube TV. “[T]here’s a certain tactical logic to seeking an injunction with a newly restored liability verdict in hand. That finding wouldn’t automatically establish that the YouTube TV arrangement is unlawful, but it would give the plaintiffs a substantial starting point. A credible threat to that relationship would rattle the NFL far more than another squabble over how much former DirecTV subscribers are owed,” Gardner writes. Should the plaintiffs pursue that avenue, a district court could begin considering paths that impact the NFL’s Sunday Ticket package right now . Obviously, that is something the league would like to avoid at all costs. This is partly why Gardner suggests the “most sensible ending” to this decade-long ordeal is an ending that, in hindsight, the league likely wishes it pursued a long time ago: a settlement. Paramount-Skydance recently closed a massive $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. and all of the company’s assets, including networks like HBO, TBS, TNT, and many others. While the UFC’s broadcast deal with Paramount that kicked off at the start of 2026 landed the majority of the organization’s programming on the Paramount+ streaming service, this merger opens the door to all sorts of possibilities. TKO Group Holdings president and COO Mark Shapiro revealed on Wednesday that talks are already ongoing about the merger and the UFC’s potential expansion to different networks. “We’re in conversation as we speak with Skydance about the best way to maximize audience across the Skydance platform,” Shapiro said during a TKO financial call. “We have a great partnership with the entire team there. I used to work with David Berson, who’s the head of Skydance Sports, from our days at ESPN. He’s super creative. “We will be maximizing HBO, TNT, Paramount+, CBS, all in the name of expanding eyeballs, expanding viewership, growing audience, and increasing engagement. Fully aligned strategically with Skydance and, frankly, they made a huge investment in UFC, and we want to see that we help them maximize their returns.” The UFC inked a huge seven-year, $7.7 billion deal to move from ESPN to Paramount at the start of 2026 while simultaneously eliminating pay-per-view broadcasts, with every event now airing exclusively on the Paramount+ streaming service. While the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. is complete, the full integration for all the various properties is still underway. Eventually, Paramount+ is expected to merge with HBO Max, and that immediately increases overall subscriptions and viewership. There’s no telling how much Paramount plans to feature the UFC on the different platforms, but obviously it sounds like that kind of programming could be happening in the near future.

item.title: Eagles reportedly making quarterback change amidst struggles
item.description: Aug 16, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles helmet on the bench during a game against the Cleveland Browns at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles’ season has been falling apart for weeks. Now they’re making a change at the most important position on the field, just two days after saying they wouldn’t. Philadelphia is turning to its third starting quarterback of the season. And it’s a player who was on another team’s practice squad less than a month ago. Eagles turn to Joe Milton Amidst a six-game losing streak, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Joe Milton will start for the Eagles against the Giants on Sunday. He’ll replace Tanner McKee, who started the last three games. That’s a sharp reversal from what Nick Sirianni said on Monday. When asked if a change at quarterback was on the table, the Eagles coach was clear. “Again, you know, Tanner’s our guy. We’re not making any changes there,” Sirianni said, in his Monday press conference . “And you know, again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme, you know, that could be within how we, you know, our schedule is, practice plays, right? And so everything’s on the table for us in that aspect.” Apparently, everything included the quarterback. McKee completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions in his three starts, according to ESPN. The Eagles lost all three. The Eagles signed Milton off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. He spent last season as Dak Prescott’s backup in Dallas after being traded there by the Patriots, who drafted him in the sixth round in 2024. On Wednesday, before the news broke, Sirianni praised Milton’s work ethic. “He works extremely hard. You know, he is, he’s always in the building, doing the extra things, and yeah, I like his progression,” Sirianni said . A season gone wrong The quarterback carousel started when Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve in October after doctors found multiple blood clots in both of his lungs. Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season. The situation drew widespread backlash after it was revealed Hurts still played after being hospitalized . The NFL was reportedly “furious” with the Eagles over how it was handled. Things haven’t gotten any better on the field. After a 2-0 start, the Eagles have dropped six straight and sit last in the NFC East at 2-6. After Sunday night’s 27-10 loss to the Commanders, Sirianni put the blame on himself , saying, “I’m not doing a good enough job right now.” The post Eagles reportedly making quarterback change amidst struggles appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

But another former New York Yankees All-Star is emerging as a potential replacement. Baltimore has been predicted to sign veteran right-hander Clay Holmes, who is back on the open market after spending the 2026 season with the New York Mets and Chicago Cubs. Holmes, a two-time All-Star with the Yankees, became a free agent after declining his $12 million player option for 2027. In his November 4 free-agent predictions, Bleacher Report’s Tim Kelly projected Holmes to sign a two-year, $48 million contract with Baltimore, including a $20 million club option for 2029. The move would give the Orioles an experienced starter as the franchise looks to strengthen its pitching staff. Orioles Predicted to Make $48 Million Move for Clay Holmes Holmes has built an unusual career, establishing himself as a dominant late-inning reliever before successfully transitioning to the starting rotation. He earned All-Star selections with New York in 2022 and 2024 before signing a three-year, $38 million contract with the Mets ahead of the 2025 season. Holmes became an immediate contributor to New York’s rotation, finishing his first season as a full-time starter with a 3.53 ERA across 165 2/3 innings. His second season began even better. Through nine starts in 2026, Holmes owned a 2.39 ERA before suffering a fractured right fibula when Yankees prospect Spencer Jones hit a 111.1 mph line drive off his leg in May. The injury sidelined Holmes for more than two months. By the time he returned, he had been traded to Chicago. His production declined with the Cubs, as he recorded a 4.62 ERA in nine starts. Nevertheless, Holmes finished the season with a respectable 3.29 ERA over 101 1/3 innings. Those results, combined with Holmes’ successful transition to starting pitching, could earn him another substantial contract. Holmes will turn 34 before the 2027 season, but his experience could make him a valuable addition for a team seeking stability.
